---
title: Datasets
llms-description: Importing Harbor task functions, pinning to a specific Harbor ref, and known dataset issues.
---

Inspect Harbor provides one task function per dataset in the [Harbor registry](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets). You can import and use them directly:

```python
from inspect_harbor import (
    aider_polyglot,
    swe_bench_verified,
    terminal_bench_2,
    aime,
    gpqa_diamond,
    usaco,
    # ... and many more
)
```

For the complete list of available datasets, see the [Registry](registry.qmd).

## Pinning

Each generated task accepts a `ref` parameter that selects which Harbor revision to load. The default is `"latest"`:

```python
from inspect_harbor import aider_polyglot

# Uses the latest revision
eval(aider_polyglot(), model="openai/gpt-5-mini")

# Pins to a specific Harbor ref (digest, revision number, or tag) for reproducibility
eval(
    aider_polyglot(
        ref="sha256:01e28d85e46beae5b7e29a29f57cb49d882b5486583d52cec4ee5bf3540a1c84",
    ),
    model="openai/gpt-5-mini",
)
```

The exact `sha256:` digest of `latest` at generation time is recorded in each task's docstring (`Latest digest:` line) and on its details page (linked from the [Registry](registry.qmd)).

## Known Issues

These are upstream issues we've encountered while integrating Harbor datasets. Each of these tasks is currently unrunnable as-is:

| Dataset | Issue | Status |
|---------|-------|--------|
| `xlang/ds-1000` | Multiple configuration issues preventing execution (`pull access denied for ds1000`) | [harbor-datasets#103](https://github.com/laude-institute/harbor-datasets/issues/103) |

## Volume mount limitations

Multi-service tasks can declare Docker `volumes:` in their `docker-compose.yaml`; single-service tasks are unaffected.

- **`${HOST_*}` log mounts become named volumes.** Harbor binds per-trial directories on the Docker host at `${HOST_VERIFIER_LOGS_PATH}`, `${HOST_AGENT_LOGS_PATH}` and `${HOST_ARTIFACTS_PATH}`. inspect_harbor has no host side (the sandbox need not be local Docker), so these expand to compose named volumes that are shared between the sample's services and removed with the sandbox. Short-form and long-form mounts of the whole directory are supported; tasks whose services exchange logs this way (`kumo/*`, `sierra-research/tau3-bench`, ...) run on local Docker and on Daytona.
- **Subpaths of `${HOST_*}` are dropped.** A mount such as `${HOST_ARTIFACTS_PATH}/out:/out` is valid against Harbor's host directory but has no named-volume equivalent. The converter drops the mount and logs a warning naming the task and service, rather than failing at `compose up`.
- **Task-file binds aren't delivered** — relative/host-path file mounts (`./setup.json`, `./AGENT.md`, `${CONTEXT_DIR}/../../shared/...`) aren't mounted into the container. Affected: `grafana/o11y-bench`, `yanagiorigami/frontier-cs`, `scale-ai/hil-bench`.

## Network isolation

`[environment].network_mode` maps onto compose `network_mode`, which is the only networking primitive every Inspect sandbox provider offers. That reproduces Harbor's egress control only partly:

- **`no-network`** sets `network_mode: none` on every service that declares no networking of its own. A service with its own `network_mode` or `networks:` keeps it, exactly as under Harbor, which routes only unconfigured services through its egress sidecar. Note what that means: a task can give a service internet access under `no-network` by declaring `network_mode: bridge` or a `networks:` block, in Harbor and here alike.
- **Sibling services are isolated from each other under `no-network`.** Harbor puts the unconfigured services into one shared egress-sidecar network namespace, so `main` still reaches a sidecar on `localhost` (verified against Harbor 0.23). With `network_mode: none` each service gets its own empty namespace, so a `no-network` task whose `main` talks to a database sidecar over `localhost` works under Harbor and fails here. Tracked in [#196](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_harbor/issues/196).
- **`allowlist`** cannot be enforced in a plain compose project and is treated as `public`; the loader logs a degraded-fidelity warning. See [#118](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_harbor/issues/118).
- **Per-phase policies** (`[agent].network_mode`, `[verifier].network_mode`) cannot be applied to a running sandbox, so the `[environment]` mode applies to both phases. The loader warns when they differ.
